opening_message:
Ticket 1: Douglas Salinas (employee ID E045) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E045.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Douglas Salinas (E045) is a full-time Engineer. Requested write access to Payroll is within the allowed maximum (write for full-time employees), so I recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record shows Douglas Salinas (E045) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training max out at read; write is above the allowed maximum, so I recommend granting read.
reason: Douglas Salinas (E045) requested write access to Payroll. The notes conflict on employment type: Note 1 says full_time (max write for full-time employees), while the Security record (Note 2) says contractor with basic security training, which caps access at read (contractors get write only with advanced training). Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, and Douglas is an Engineer, so admin is not available either way. Given the Security record identifying him as a contractor with basic training, write exceeds the maximum; granting the maximum (read).
